configuration_note: Single NUMA 0, 28 CPU threads, CUDA 0/1 serial layer map, per-device 8 GiB expert cache, fast prefill, 8600 input tokens, chunk 4096; draft weights loaded but speculation and prefix/history reuse disabled per request.
timing_note: TTFT medians of three ordinary one-output-token requests. Native phases are means of those requests; operator times are means of two separately synchronized profiles. Join is residual GPU wait after concurrent CPU work, not pure GPU compute time. NVFP4 whole-model numbers reuse the prior same-configuration baseline.
implementation: Scale the Q2_K_R4/Q4_K_R4 restore launch grid to the GPU SM count.

Use 64-row MMQ compute tiles for V4.1 batches of at least 1024 rows, retaining 16-row route padding and unchanged workspace capacity. Clamp activation reads at expert tails; existing write-back bounds discard padded outputs.

Upload gate/up on the caller stream; upload and restore down weights on a high-priority nonblocking stream while gate/up computes. Events protect descriptor lifetime, down-weight readiness, and staging reuse. Extra device scratch is one projection, 7.38 MiB for this model.

validation.cuda_memcheck_case: Static test executable, host 256 256 1041, both GPUs, wide-tile tail and asynchronous uploads.
validation.sanitizer_note: The first attempt against the dynamic microbenchmark could not initialize the sanitizer (CUDA initialized before injection). The static test run completed with instrumentation and zero errors.
validation.precision_note: Includes newly added 1023/1024/1041-row cases, so the maximum spans more fixtures than the previous report. Both GPUs produce bitwise-identical BF16 microbenchmark outputs to the previous library at 4096 and 128 rows.

memory.device_mapping: CUDA 0 = physical index 1 RTX 4090; CUDA 1 = physical index 0 RTX 4090 D.

limitations: Synthetic GPU fixtures fix routing and weights, omit concurrent CPU experts and full-model memory pressure, and are not a cross-format model-accuracy comparison.
Kernel duration sums include overlap with other kernels and transfers. End-to-end speedups must use wall-clock measurements.
Accuracy checks are operator references and a long retrieval request, not a full perplexity evaluation.
